findings.finding: Production probability law uses `std::log`/`std::exp` (platform libm) with double rounding into Q16. Encoder and decoder must use bit-identical libm. Safe on one machine, but a cross-machine or cross-libc decode (the lexth11c README tests an AMD leg) can desynchronize. Use integer stretch/squash tables, as paq/cmix do.
findings.correction: New mixer probability generation and updates are integer-only; floating logarithms score diagnostics only.
findings.remaining_requirement: This is a new law, not a bit-identical replacement of old floating fixed-share code; native Linux quality and decode remain required.

findings.finding: Source patching by literal string replacement, then `exec(..., globals())`. See E2.

findings.finding: Parity compared on float16-stored probabilities (`'<f2'`). Adequate for the observed failure size, but sub-6e-5 probabilities are subnormal and lose relative precision. A KL ≤ 1e-5 gate was specified against data whose storage noise floor is never stated.
findings.correction: Precision/fidelity work uses FP32 native distributions or exact Q16 traces; fp16 probes cannot resolve a sub-noise KL gate.
findings.remaining_requirement: Old fp16 probe results retain their storage limitation.

findings.finding: Context hash tables without check bytes: collisions silently merge contexts. Acceptable for a stand-in, but the stand-in's weakness (1.82–1.89 bpb) drove "blend" conclusions in rounds 2–4.
